visibleInputs: sources/ and people.json of the demo, train and validation families (demo seeded by demo:reset --synthetic, train and validation arriving during the day as demo:play sends them)
incoming problem text and observations (asked by simulated engineers)
hypothesis: A simulated day of questions answered by simulated colleagues raises the store metric (completeness x correctness, BUILD_BRIEF 5.1-5.2) of the demo store, and the LinUCB selector rewarded by the measured delta of that metric minus burden (5.4) gains at least as much per question asked as the rules selector on the same store and the same day.

variants.description: rules selector (the fixed prior); the coordinator still writes the measured reward
LinUCB (alpha 0.5, fresh per seed), updated live after every answer with the store-metric reward

config.store: Engine on :memory:, demo:reset --synthetic (the Elisa files are absent here), clock frozen at 2026-11-09T07:00Z and moved only by the simulated day
config.day: simulation/schedule.ts planDay (10 h, seeded) + simulation/runner.ts runDay against the real service through createDispatcher (in-process, no socket); simulated colleagues answer from a seeded model, never from answer keys; no judge prompts
config.reward: QuestionCoordinator.answer: delta of completeness x correctness of the touched case before and after the answer, minus burden (0.02 per question asked today, 0.02 per other open question); selector.update after each answer (store-metric-delta@1); an applicability answer is not a source for or against the case's claims (D-B2-66)
config.ranking: rules selector: value / cost among the pairs that pass the gate (D-B2-67)
config.metric: memory/store-health.ts storeHealth over every case (no principal); completenessUnweighted is compared before/after because the weighted mean needs retrievals, which only exist after the day
config.questionsPerPoint: questions asked / (100 x the gain in completenessUnweighted x correctness over the cases that existed before the day); null when there is no gain

acceptanceCriteria: Report before/after per seed and the mean over 3 seeds, with every denominator (cases, case claims, questions).

Bandit vs rules: LinUCB is reported as better only if its mean same-case gain per question asked is higher than the rules selector's on at least 2 of 3 seeds; otherwise the rules selector stays the default (it is the default either way until a judge-visible reason exists).
